title: Reconcile Project Members (.dpr/.dproj)
summary: Compares a project file's declared member list against what is on disk and in the compile closure
intro: Read this after moving or adding units by hand. It compares the project file declared members against what is on disk and in the compile closure, and with --apply it syncs the list; without --apply it only reports.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Reconcile Project Members (.dpr/.dproj)...
steps: Open the project in RAD Studio
Choose drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Reconcile Project Members (.dpr/.dproj)...
Review the missing and stale entries it reports; nothing is written until you apply

surfaces.usage: drag-lint reconcile-project <App.dpr|.dproj> [--apply] [--only <unit,...>] [--db <db>] [--full] [--json] [--config <path>] - sync project member list; flag stale used units. --only restricts MISSING (and therefore --apply) to a reviewed selection, so a dry run with --only previews exactly what --apply would write. --json carries `applied` (the OUTCOME, false when --apply had nothing to write) plus `backups` and `edited` when --apply is passed
help: drag-lint reconcile-project <App.dpr|.dproj> [--apply] [--only <unit,...>] [--db <db>] [--full] [--json] [--config <path>]  - sync project member list; flag stale used units. --only restricts MISSING (and therefore --apply) to a reviewed selection, so a dry run with --only previews exactly what --apply would write. --json carries `applied` (the OUTCOME, false when --apply had nothing to write) plus `backups` and `edited` when --apply is passed
--db heals the index+findings for every project member (re-scan + recompile) WITHOUT editing the .dpr; --full forces the recompile even when nothing is incoherent

questions.ask: Does my .dproj list every unit the project actually uses?
How do I add the missing units to the project file?
